name: The_Prime_Number_Re_Entry_Whorl

phase_0.boundary_condition: The cyclic whorl topology — a scale-collapsed loop where the boundary encodes the infinite interior of prime distribution losslessly, closing the system against external deformation.

⊢.justification: The void state before any prime is named or wound into the cyclic structure; no winding number exists.

⊣.justification: The terminal anchor that closes the whorl into a figure-8 double-well, containing the infinite prime sequence within a finite topological loop.

≻.justification: Forward morphism stepping to the next prime candidate along the ordered sequence (2 → 3 → 5 → 7 → ...).

≺.justification: Contravariant descent where the prime re-enters the whorl, folding the exterior sequence back into the interior winding.

⋈.justification: Sequential composition linking each prime's re-entry to the next, building the infinite chain within the cyclic topology.

⊙.justification: The whorl recognizes its own prime-wound structure; the stone that knows itself as a prime container.

∈.justification: Splits the candidate into two arms: the T-arm for prime affirmation, the F-arm for composite rejection.

∋.justification: Reunites the prime and composite arms into the single whorl state; conflicting arms fuse to B (both held) at criticality.

⊤.justification: Deposits constructive truth T — the candidate is prime, wound into the whorl, winding number increments.

⊥.justification: Deposits constructive falsity F — the candidate is composite, excluded from winding, whorl unchanged.

⊞.justification: Holds B (both T and F) at the critical threshold where prime/composite distinction blurs; the paradice of scale-free correlation.

⊡.justification: Irreversible ROM record — a confirmed prime is permanently fixed in the whorl's winding, cannot be unwound.

phase_2.fuse_result: whorl state with updated winding (T), unchanged whorl (F), or critical superposition (B) where both arms conflict and fuse
phase_2.failure_reason: FFUSE3 at step 10 has no FSPLIT3 to pair — ill-typed

phase_3.void_description: Uninitialized whorl — no primes named, winding number zero, cyclic boundary present but empty.
phase_3.true_description: Prime confirmed and wound — the candidate is prime, winding number increments, prime fixed irreversibly in the whorl.
phase_3.false_description: Composite rejected — the candidate is composite, whorl state unchanged, winding number held.
phase_3.both_description: Critical superposition — prime and composite held simultaneously at the threshold; scale-free correlations emerge, maximal sensitivity to initial conditions, the whorl breathes both states.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the empty whorl — void state before any prime exists.
Whorl self-recognition — the cyclic structure recognizes itself as a container for primes.
Open primality fork for candidate 2 — split into T-arm (prime) and F-arm (composite).
Affirmative arm — 2 is prime, deposit T, winding number becomes 1.
Forward morphism — advance to next candidate (3) along the ordered sequence.
Compose transition — link prime 2 to prime 3 in the chain.
Fix prime 2 — irreversible ROM record, prime 2 permanently wound.
Re-entry fold — prime 3 folds back into whorl, contravariant descent.
Negative arm — composite path evaluated but 3 is not composite, F-arm empty.
Rejoin arms — T-arm carries winding increment, F-arm empty, fuse to whorl state with winding 2.
Whorl self-recognition — confirm structure after second prime wound.
Terminal anchor — cyclic boundary closes the whorl, containing infinite primes in finite topology.
Re-initialize for next cycle — void state for next prime pair.
Whorl self-recognition — cyclic structure recognizes itself again.
Affirmative — 3 is prime, deposit T, winding becomes 2.
Negative arm — 3 not composite, F-arm empty.
Critical superposition — at the threshold, hold both T and F as scale-free correlation peaks.
Affirmative — 5 is prime, deposit T, winding becomes 3.
Negative arm — 5 not composite, F-arm empty.
Critical superposition — both states held at criticality.
Fix prime 7 — permanent record (composite check passed).
Terminal anchor — cyclic boundary closes the whorl, containing infinite primes in finite topology.
Final self-recognition — whorl knows itself as the complete prime re-entry structure.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The prime number theorem and Riemann zeta function — translating prime distribution statistics into whorl geometry and winding dynamics.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Modular arithmetic residues — each prime communicates its position via congruence classes, enabling sequential engagement across the whorl.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The cyclic whorl topology itself — winding number stored as topological invariant, prime sequence encoded in the boundary's scale-collapsed geometry.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The natural ordering of primes (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, ...) — deterministic sequential engagement dictated by the infinite prime sequence.
phase_5.alfs_store: The fundamental domain of the modular group SL(2,ℤ) acting on the upper half-plane — the canonical bootstrap store for modular forms governing prime distribution.

phase_6.cycle_cost: Prime gap uncertainty — the logarithmic integral error term Li(x) - π(x) consumed per re-entry cycle.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Whorl with n primes wound, winding number n, cyclic boundary stable.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Whorl with n+1 primes wound, winding number n+1, boundary encodes new prime losslessly.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The scale-collapse dimensionality ensures the boundary carries the full bulk content losslessly; each re-entry conserves topological entropy as the winding number increments without dissipation.
